concepts.title: What is Factorisation
concepts.formula: factorisation: expression = product of irreducible factors

questions.q: Evaluate 3x + 3 when x = 8.
Find the value of 3x^2 + 7x + 5 when x = 3.
Simplify 8x + 7x - 8x and give the coefficient of x.
Use the distributive law: 9 x (7 + 9) equals 9 x 7 + 9 x 9. Compute it.
Evaluate 8 + 2 x 2 (respect the order of operations).
Evaluate (3 + 6) x 8.

concepts.title: Method of Common Factors
concepts.formula: common factor: a x m + a x n = a x (m + n)

questions.q: Two numbers 14 and 28 have HCF 7 with coprime multipliers 2 and 4. Verify by computing hcf = 7 x 1; then find the HCF value.
Find the LCM of 14 and 28 given their HCF is 7 and HCF x LCM = product of the numbers.
The LCM of 14 and 28 is 56. Use HCF x LCM = a x b to find their HCF.
Two ropes of lengths 14 cm and 28 cm are cut into equal pieces of greatest length. What is the length of each piece?
Two bells ring together now. They ring at intervals of 14 minutes and 28 minutes. After how many minutes will they next ring together?
How many multiples of 12 are there up to 96?

concepts.title: Factorisation by Regrouping
concepts.formula: group terms -> common factor of each group -> common bracket factor

questions.q: For the digits 6, 9, 7, 7 form the largest and smallest 4-digit numbers and find their difference (Kaprekar step).
The number 8726 is split into landmark groups of 1000, 100 and 10. How many complete 1000-groups does it contain?
Find the digit sum of 8726.
Find the remainder when the digit sum of 8726 (= 23) is divided by 9.
Take the 2-digit number 28, reverse its digits to get 82, and find the positive difference (a Kaprekar-style step).
For the 2-digit number 28 (digits 2 and 8), the difference between the number and its reversal is always 9 x (difference of digits). Compute that difference.
Use the identity (a + b)^2 = a^2 + 2ab + b^2 to find the square of 9 more than 8; report the value.
Using (a - b)^2 = a^2 - 2ab + b^2, evaluate 24^2 - 2 x 24 x 9 + 9^2.
Use a^2 - b^2 = (a + b)(a - b) to compute 15 x 9 where the numbers are a + b and a - b for a = 12, b = 3.
Expand (x + 2)(x + 3) using the identity x^2 + (a + b)x + ab and evaluate it at x = 8.
Evaluate 98 x 102 using a^2 - b^2 with a = 100 and b = 2.

concepts.title: Factors of the Form (x + a)(x + b)
concepts.formula: (x + a)(x + b) = x^2 + (a + b)x + ab; find ab = q and a + b = p

questions.q: Use the identity (a + b)^2 = a^2 + 2ab + b^2 to find the square of 3 more than 12; report the value.
Using (a - b)^2 = a^2 - 2ab + b^2, evaluate 25^2 - 2 x 25 x 2 + 2^2.
Use a^2 - b^2 = (a + b)(a - b) to compute 14 x 6 where the numbers are a + b and a - b for a = 10, b = 4.
Expand (x + 5)(x + 5) using the identity x^2 + (a + b)x + ab and evaluate it at x = 6.
Evaluate 98 x 102 using a^2 - b^2 with a = 100 and b = 2.

concepts.title: Division of a Monomial by a Monomial

questions.q: Using the law a^m x a^n = a^(m+n), evaluate 4^2 x 4^4.
Using a^m / a^n = a^(m-n), evaluate 3^6 / 3^2.
Evaluate (4^2)^3 using the power of a power law.
Evaluate 3^2 x 4^2 using a^m x b^m = (ab)^m.
Find the value of 4^0.
Evaluate 9^(-2) and give the value as a fraction.

concepts.title: Division of a Polynomial by a Monomial
concepts.formula: divide each term of the polynomial by the monomial

questions.q: Evaluate 3x + 2 when x = 4.
Find the value of 5x^2 + 6x + 5 when x = 4.
Simplify 8x + 5x - 5x and give the coefficient of x.
Use the distributive law: 9 x (5 + 8) equals 9 x 5 + 9 x 8. Compute it.
Evaluate 2 + 8 x 2 (respect the order of operations).
Evaluate (8 + 4) x 3.

concepts.title: Division of a Polynomial by a Polynomial
concepts.formula: factorise both polynomials and cancel common factors; dividend = divisor x quotient

questions.q: Two numbers 24 and 36 have HCF 12 with coprime multipliers 2 and 3. Verify by computing hcf = 12 x 1; then find the HCF value.
Find the LCM of 24 and 36 given their HCF is 12 and HCF x LCM = product of the numbers.
The LCM of 24 and 36 is 72. Use HCF x LCM = a x b to find their HCF.
Two ropes of lengths 24 cm and 36 cm are cut into equal pieces of greatest length. What is the length of each piece?
Two bells ring together now. They ring at intervals of 24 minutes and 36 minutes. After how many minutes will they next ring together?
How many multiples of 18 are there up to 120?
